discussion.text: Make a small 2D side-view jump game called Bridge Runner. Keyboard left/right and space jump; cross three visible platforms to a green exit, falling restarts, R resets, HUD explains controls and win. Use simple procedural shapes, no external assets/plugins/network. Fixed 960x540 camera, single level, no sound. Represent the player as object id player with editable numeric speed (220, min 50, max 500) and jump-speed (420, min 200, max 700). Represent the main scene as main-scene bound to scenes/main.tscn. Make each mechanism/object explicit with stable IDs and source bindings. This fully specified isolated test authorizes the MVP plan; do not ask optional questions, use READY unless a real blocker exists.

discussion.summary: Bridge Runner has a complete isolated MVP plan: one fixed 960x540 level, three visible platforms, keyboard movement and jumping, a green exit, automatic restart after falling, R to reset, and a controls/win HUD. Procedural shapes keep the scope self-contained. Platform reachability remains a manual playtest item. READY indicates planning readiness for this isolated test only; it does not grant production approval or claim verified behavior.

requirements.text: Implement one Godot 4 GDScript 2D level with procedural visuals, no sound, no external assets or plugins, and no network access.
The main-scene object is bound to scenes/main.tscn. Keep every declared object and mechanism associated with its listed source bindings.

Preserve player field IDs speed and jump-speed. Speed is editable numeric data with value 220, minimum 50, maximum 500. Jump-speed is editable numeric data with value 420, minimum 200, maximum 700. Game source reads these frozen values through StudioRuntime.object_value(). Do not modify backend-owned design/game.json or studio/runtime.gd.
Left and Right Arrow move the player horizontally; Space triggers a grounded jump; R resets the level. Opposing direction inputs cancel, and holding Space does not produce repeated jumps.

Show exactly three solid platforms simultaneously. At the default player field values, the player can jump from the starting platform to the middle platform and then to the exit platform. Manually assess reachability and adjust platform spacing if needed while retaining the specified player defaults.
The player lands reliably on matching platform collision shapes and can fall through the open gaps. Grounded detection permits jumping only while supported.
Place a clearly visible green exit on the third platform. Player overlap changes the level to won, stops player movement, and displays a win message with an R restart instruction.
Falling below the level during play automatically restores the initial spawn, zero velocity, playing state, and normal HUD.
R restores the same initial state during play and after winning. The player can complete another attempt after either reset path.
Use a fixed 960x540 logical view with all three platforms and the exit visible together. The view does not follow the player or scroll.
The HUD explains arrow movement, Space jumping, R reset, and the green-exit goal. Win feedback is readable and does not obscure the platform route.
Keep physics and level simulation separate from input action mapping, procedural rendering, and interface updates. Input supplies intent; rendering reflects state; HUD presents controls and outcomes.

requirements.text: Implement one Godot 4 GDScript 2D level with procedural visuals, no sound, no external assets or plugins, and no network access.
The main-scene object is bound to scenes/main.tscn. Keep every declared object and mechanism associated with its listed source bindings.

Preserve player field IDs speed and jump-speed. Speed is editable numeric data with value 220, minimum 50, maximum 500. Jump-speed is editable numeric data with value 420, minimum 200, maximum 700. Game source reads these frozen values through StudioRuntime.object_value(). Do not modify backend-owned design/game.json or studio/runtime.gd.
Left and Right Arrow move the player horizontally; Space triggers a grounded jump; R resets the level. Opposing direction inputs cancel, and holding Space does not produce repeated jumps.

Show exactly three solid platforms simultaneously. At the default player field values, the player can jump from the starting platform to the middle platform and then to the exit platform. Manually assess reachability and adjust platform spacing if needed while retaining the specified player defaults.
The player lands reliably on matching platform collision shapes and can fall through the open gaps. Grounded detection permits jumping only while supported.
Place a clearly visible green exit on the third platform. Player overlap changes the level to won, stops player movement, and displays a win message with an R restart instruction.
Falling below the level during play automatically restores the initial spawn, zero velocity, playing state, and normal HUD.
R restores the same initial state during play and after winning. The player can complete another attempt after either reset path.
Use a fixed 960x540 logical view with all three platforms and the exit visible together. The view does not follow the player or scroll.
The HUD explains arrow movement, Space jumping, R reset, and the green-exit goal. Win feedback is readable and does not obscure the platform route.
Keep physics and level simulation separate from input action mapping, procedural rendering, and interface updates. Input supplies intent; rendering reflects state; HUD presents controls and outcomes.

tasks.description: In the isolated implementation stage, create scenes/main.tscn and configure the fixed 960x540 view. Establish the declared scene hierarchy and source bindings.
Implement the four keyboard actions and provide movement, jump, and reset intent to simulation code.
Implement player movement, gravity, grounded jumping, and collision response. Read speed and jump-speed through StudioRuntime.object_value() using the declared frozen fields.
Create the three platforms with the proposed positions and matching collision shapes, the initial player spawn, and the green exit trigger on the third platform.
Implement playing and won states, exit detection, automatic fall restart, and R reset through one shared restart path. Restore player velocity, spawn, controls, and HUD state consistently.
Draw simple readable shapes for the player, platforms, background, and green exit using Godot primitives, with no external assets.
Add the controls, goal, EXIT label, and win/restart feedback. Position interface text away from the playable route.

During the isolated implementation stage, manually exercise the complete route at default field values, landing, falling, R during play, winning, and R after winning. Inspect HUD readability and fixed-view visibility. Check that edited speed and jump-speed values are consumed through the runtime accessor. Record observed results without treating test readiness as production approval.

proposal.text: Make a small 2D side-view jump game called Bridge Runner. Keyboard left/right and space jump; cross three visible platforms to a green exit, falling restarts, R resets, HUD explains controls and win. Use simple procedural shapes, no external assets/plugins/network. Fixed 960x540 camera, single level, no sound. Represent the player as object id player with editable numeric speed (220, min 50, max 500) and jump-speed (420, min 200, max 700). Represent the main scene as main-scene bound to scenes/main.tscn. Make each mechanism/object explicit with stable IDs and source bindings. This fully specified isolated test authorizes the MVP plan; do not ask optional questions, use READY unless a real blocker exists.

requirements.text: Implement one Godot 4 GDScript 2D level with procedural visuals, no sound, no external assets or plugins, and no network access.
The main-scene object is bound to scenes/main.tscn. Keep every declared object and mechanism associated with its listed source bindings.

Preserve player field IDs speed and jump-speed. Speed is editable numeric data with value 220, minimum 50, maximum 500. Jump-speed is editable numeric data with value 420, minimum 200, maximum 700. Game source reads these frozen values through StudioRuntime.object_value(). Do not modify backend-owned design/game.json or studio/runtime.gd.
Left and Right Arrow move the player horizontally; Space triggers a grounded jump; R resets the level. Opposing direction inputs cancel, and holding Space does not produce repeated jumps.

Show exactly three solid platforms simultaneously. At the default player field values, the player can jump from the starting platform to the middle platform and then to the exit platform. Manually assess reachability and adjust platform spacing if needed while retaining the specified player defaults.
The player lands reliably on matching platform collision shapes and can fall through the open gaps. Grounded detection permits jumping only while supported.
Place a clearly visible green exit on the third platform. Player overlap changes the level to won, stops player movement, and displays a win message with an R restart instruction.
Falling below the level during play automatically restores the initial spawn, zero velocity, playing state, and normal HUD.
R restores the same initial state during play and after winning. The player can complete another attempt after either reset path.
Use a fixed 960x540 logical view with all three platforms and the exit visible together. The view does not follow the player or scroll.
The HUD explains arrow movement, Space jumping, R reset, and the green-exit goal. Win feedback is readable and does not obscure the platform route.
Keep physics and level simulation separate from input action mapping, procedural rendering, and interface updates. Input supplies intent; rendering reflects state; HUD presents controls and outcomes.

approvedProposal.summary: Bridge Runner has a complete isolated MVP plan: one fixed 960x540 level, three visible platforms, keyboard movement and jumping, a green exit, automatic restart after falling, R to reset, and a controls/win HUD. Procedural shapes keep the scope self-contained. Platform reachability remains a manual playtest item. READY indicates planning readiness for this isolated test only; it does not grant production approval or claim verified behavior.

tasks.description: In the isolated implementation stage, create scenes/main.tscn and configure the fixed 960x540 view. Establish the declared scene hierarchy and source bindings.
Implement the four keyboard actions and provide movement, jump, and reset intent to simulation code.
Implement player movement, gravity, grounded jumping, and collision response. Read speed and jump-speed through StudioRuntime.object_value() using the declared frozen fields.
Create the three platforms with the proposed positions and matching collision shapes, the initial player spawn, and the green exit trigger on the third platform.
Implement playing and won states, exit detection, automatic fall restart, and R reset through one shared restart path. Restore player velocity, spawn, controls, and HUD state consistently.
Draw simple readable shapes for the player, platforms, background, and green exit using Godot primitives, with no external assets.
Add the controls, goal, EXIT label, and win/restart feedback. Position interface text away from the playable route.

During the isolated implementation stage, manually exercise the complete route at default field values, landing, falling, R during play, winning, and R after winning. Inspect HUD readability and fixed-view visibility. Check that edited speed and jump-speed values are consumed through the runtime accessor. Record observed results without treating test readiness as production approval.

approvedProposal.text: Make a small 2D side-view jump game called Bridge Runner. Keyboard left/right and space jump; cross three visible platforms to a green exit, falling restarts, R resets, HUD explains controls and win. Use simple procedural shapes, no external assets/plugins/network. Fixed 960x540 camera, single level, no sound. Represent the player as object id player with editable numeric speed (220, min 50, max 500) and jump-speed (420, min 200, max 700). Represent the main scene as main-scene bound to scenes/main.tscn. Make each mechanism/object explicit with stable IDs and source bindings. This fully specified isolated test authorizes the MVP plan; do not ask optional questions, use READY unless a real blocker exists.

userAcceptance.text: Implement one Godot 4 GDScript 2D level with procedural visuals, no sound, no external assets or plugins, and no network access.
The main-scene object is bound to scenes/main.tscn. Keep every declared object and mechanism associated with its listed source bindings.

Preserve player field IDs speed and jump-speed. Speed is editable numeric data with value 220, minimum 50, maximum 500. Jump-speed is editable numeric data with value 420, minimum 200, maximum 700. Game source reads these frozen values through StudioRuntime.object_value(). Do not modify backend-owned design/game.json or studio/runtime.gd.
Left and Right Arrow move the player horizontally; Space triggers a grounded jump; R resets the level. Opposing direction inputs cancel, and holding Space does not produce repeated jumps.

Show exactly three solid platforms simultaneously. At the default player field values, the player can jump from the starting platform to the middle platform and then to the exit platform. Manually assess reachability and adjust platform spacing if needed while retaining the specified player defaults.
The player lands reliably on matching platform collision shapes and can fall through the open gaps. Grounded detection permits jumping only while supported.
Place a clearly visible green exit on the third platform. Player overlap changes the level to won, stops player movement, and displays a win message with an R restart instruction.
Falling below the level during play automatically restores the initial spawn, zero velocity, playing state, and normal HUD.
R restores the same initial state during play and after winning. The player can complete another attempt after either reset path.
Use a fixed 960x540 logical view with all three platforms and the exit visible together. The view does not follow the player or scroll.
The HUD explains arrow movement, Space jumping, R reset, and the green-exit goal. Win feedback is readable and does not obscure the platform route.
Keep physics and level simulation separate from input action mapping, procedural rendering, and interface updates. Input supplies intent; rendering reflects state; HUD presents controls and outcomes.

# Game Design Document — Bridge Runner

## Concept
A small Godot 4 GDScript side-view jump game. Move with the left/right arrow keys and jump with Space to cross three visible platforms and reach a green exit. Falling restarts the level, and R resets it at any time. Use a fixed 960x540 view, procedural shapes, one level, and no sound, external assets, plugins, or network access. Keep simulation, input actions, rendering, and interface responsibilities separate.

## Object Model
- `bridge-runner` (project): Bridge Runner. A self-contained Godot 4 GDScript 2D MVP with a single playable level. Sources: not bound yet.
- `main-scene` (scene): Main Scene. Contains the player, three platforms, exit, procedural renderer, and HUD. Coordinates level state and restart behavior. Sources: scenes/main.tscn, scripts/level_controller.gd.
- `input-actions` (mechanic): Keyboard Input Actions. Define move_left for Left Arrow, move_right for Right Arrow, jump for Space, and reset_level for R. Translate input into movement, jump, and reset intent. Sources: scripts/input_actions.gd.
- `player` (entity): Player. A 24x32 rectangular CharacterBody2D. Start centered at (100, 414) on the first platform. Read speed and jump-speed from the frozen fields through StudioRuntime.object_value(). Sources: scenes/main.tscn, scripts/player.gd.
- `player.speed` (number): Speed; current value `220`; editable `true`.
- `player.jump-speed` (number): Jump Speed; current value `420`; editable `true`.
- `horizontal-movement` (mechanic): Horizontal Movement. Apply left/right intent using the player's speed field. Stop horizontal movement when neither direction is held; opposing inputs cancel. Sources: scripts/player.gd.
- `jump` (mechanic): Grounded Jump. A fresh Space press while grounded sets upward velocity from jump-speed. Apply gravity of 1000 px/s² during physics updates. Holding Space does not cause repeated jumps. Sources: scripts/player.gd.
- `platform-one` (entity): Starting Platform. A visible solid rectangle at (40, 430), sized 260x24 pixels. Holds the initial player spawn. Sources: scenes/main.tscn.
- `platform-two` (entity): Middle Platform. A visible solid rectangle at (370, 350), sized 210x24 pixels. Provides the intermediate jump destination. Sources: scenes/main.tscn.
- `platform-three` (entity): Exit Platform. A visible solid rectangle at (650, 410), sized 270x24 pixels. Supports the green exit. Sources: scenes/main.tscn.
- `platform-collision` (rule): Solid Platform Collision. Use static platform collision shapes matching the rendered rectangles. Player physics handles landing and grounded detection. Gaps remain open, with no invisible floor. Sources: scenes/main.tscn, scripts/player.gd.
- `exit` (entity): Green Exit. A green rectangular Area2D at (860, 350), sized 40x60 pixels, resting on the third platform. Label it EXIT. Sources: scenes/main.tscn, scripts/level_controller.gd.
- `win` (mechanic): Reach Exit. When the player overlaps the exit during play, enter the won state, stop player motion, and display the win message and R restart instruction. Sources: scripts/level_controller.gd.
- `fall-restart` (mechanic): Fall Restart. During play, restart when the player's center passes y=600. Return to the initial spawn and clear velocity and level state. Sources: scripts/level_controller.gd.
- `manual-reset` (mechanic): R Reset. R restores the initial level state from either playing or won state, including spawn, zero velocity, active controls, and the normal HUD. Sources: scripts/level_controller.gd.
- `level-state` (rule): Level State. Maintain playing and won states. Use one restart path for falling and R. Evaluate reset before other transitions; suppress falling and movement after winning until reset. Sources: scripts/level_controller.gd.
- `fixed-view` (rule): Fixed View. Use a fixed 960x540 logical viewport showing the entire level. Do not follow the player or scroll. Preserve aspect ratio when the window changes size. Sources: scenes/main.tscn, scripts/view_setup.gd.
- `procedural-rendering` (mechanic): Procedural Shapes. Render the background, player, platforms, and green exit using simple Godot shapes and colors. Keep drawing separate from physics, input handling, and HUD text. Sources: scenes/main.tscn, scripts/procedural_visuals.gd.
- `hud` (interface): Controls and Win HUD. Show: Left/Right: move \| Space: jump \| R: reset. Explain the goal: Cross the platforms to the green exit. On victory, show: You win! Press R to restart. Keep text clear of the jump route. Sources: scenes/main.tscn, scripts/hud.gd.

## Requirements
- `supported-scope`: Implement one Godot 4 GDScript 2D level with procedural visuals, no sound, no external assets or plugins, and no network access. (objects: bridge-runner, main-scene, procedural-rendering; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `scene-binding`: The main-scene object is bound to scenes/main.tscn. Keep every declared object and mechanism associated with its listed source bindings. (objects: main-scene; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `player-fields`: Preserve player field IDs speed and jump-speed. Speed is editable numeric data with value 220, minimum 50, maximum 500. Jump-speed is editable numeric data with value 420, minimum 200, maximum 700. Game source reads these frozen values through StudioRuntime.object_value(). Do not modify backend-owned design/game.json or studio/runtime.gd. (objects: player, horizontal-movement, jump; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `keyboard-controls`: Left and Right Arrow move the player horizontally; Space triggers a grounded jump; R resets the level. Opposing direction inputs cancel, and holding Space does not produce repeated jumps. (objects: input-actions, horizontal-movement, jump, manual-reset; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `three-platform-route`: Show exactly three solid platforms simultaneously. At the default player field values, the player can jump from the starting platform to the middle platform and then to the exit platform. Manually assess reachability and adjust platform spacing if needed while retaining the specified player defaults. (objects: player, jump, platform-one, platform-two, platform-three, platform-collision; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `solid-landings`: The player lands reliably on matching platform collision shapes and can fall through the open gaps. Grounded detection permits jumping only while supported. (objects: player, jump, platform-collision; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `green-exit-win`: Place a clearly visible green exit on the third platform. Player overlap changes the level to won, stops player movement, and displays a win message with an R restart instruction. (objects: exit, win, level-state, hud; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `fall-recovery`: Falling below the level during play automatically restores the initial spawn, zero velocity, playing state, and normal HUD. (objects: player, fall-restart, level-state, hud; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `reset-recovery`: R restores the same initial state during play and after winning. The player can complete another attempt after either reset path. (objects: manual-reset, level-state, player, hud; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `fixed-camera`: Use a fixed 960x540 logical view with all three platforms and the exit visible together. The view does not follow the player or scroll. (objects: fixed-view, main-scene; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `hud-guidance`: The HUD explains arrow movement, Space jumping, R reset, and the green-exit goal. Win feedback is readable and does not obscure the platform route. (objects: hud, win; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `separate-responsibilities`: Keep physics and level simulation separate from input action mapping, procedural rendering, and interface updates. Input supplies intent; rendering reflects state; HUD presents controls and outcomes. (objects: player, level-state, input-actions, procedural-rendering, hud; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).

## Scope and Evidence
The object document is the structured source of intent. Planning questions must be resolved before implementation. Technical smoke cannot claim unobserved game behavior; human acceptance remains a separate user decision.

## Protected bridge from game code to the server-owned object document.
## Generated game scripts should read declared values through this API.

static func value(document: Dictionary, object_id: String, field_id: String, default_value: Variant = null) -> Variant:
	for object_value in document.get("objects", []):
		if not object_value is Dictionary or object_value.get("id") != object_id:
			continue
		for field_value in object_value.get("fields", []):
			if field_value is Dictionary and field_value.get("id") == field_id:
				return field_value.get("value", default_value)
	return default_value


func object_value(object_id: String, field_id: String, default_value: Variant = null) -> Variant:
	var file := FileAccess.open("res://design/game.json", FileAccess.READ)
	if file == null:
		return default_value
	var parsed: Variant = JSON.parse_string(file.get_as_text())
	if not parsed is Dictionary:
		return default_value
	return value(parsed, object_id, field_id, default_value)

- `jump` (mechanic): Grounded Jump. A fresh Space press while grounded sets upward velocity from jump-speed. Apply gravity of 1000 px/s² during physics updates. Holding Space does not cause repeated jumps. Sources: scripts/player.gd.

## Object player; mechanisms horizontal-movement, jump, platform-collision.
## The controller supplies intent and owns the timing of each simulation step.
const OBJECT_ID := "player"
const MECHANISM_IDS := ["horizontal-movement", "jump", "platform-collision"]
const GRAVITY := 1000.0
const RuntimeSource = preload("res://studio/runtime.gd")

var speed: float = 0.0
var jump_speed: float = 0.0
var controls_enabled: bool = false
var _studio_runtime = RuntimeSource.new()


func reset_to(spawn: Vector2) -> void:
	global_position = spawn
	velocity = Vector2.ZERO
	# Read the authoritative fields on startup and on both restart paths.
	# Do not duplicate their defaults or ranges in game source.
	var speed_value: Variant = _studio_runtime.object_value(OBJECT_ID, "speed")
	var jump_value: Variant = _studio_runtime.object_value(OBJECT_ID, "jump-speed")
	controls_enabled = (
		(speed_value is int or speed_value is float)
		and (jump_value is int or jump_value is float)
	)
	if not controls_enabled:
		push_error("Player requires numeric speed and jump-speed fields in design/game.json.")
		return
	speed = float(speed_value)
	jump_speed = float(jump_value)


func simulate(delta: float, direction: float, jump_pressed: bool) -> void:
	if not controls_enabled:
		return
	# horizontal-movement: immediate start/stop, with no residual drift.
	velocity.x = direction * speed
	# jump: only a fresh press on a supporting platform starts a jump.
	velocity.y += GRAVITY * delta
	if jump_pressed and is_on_floor():
		velocity.y = -jump_speed
	# platform-collision: use the scene's matching solid collision rectangles.
	move_and_slide()


func stop_motion() -> void:
	controls_enabled = false
	velocity = Vector2.ZERO

## Object procedural-rendering: drawing only, with no collision or input logic.
## Visual children inherit their entity's transform from scenes/main.tscn.
const OBJECT_ID := "procedural-rendering"

@export_enum("background", "platform", "player", "exit")
var shape_kind: String = "platform"
@export var shape_size: Vector2 = Vector2.ZERO
@export var fill_color: Color = Color.WHITE
@export var accent_color: Color = Color.WHITE


func _draw() -> void:
	match shape_kind:
		"background":
			_draw_background()
		"platform":
			_draw_platform()
		"player":
			_draw_player()
		"exit":
			_draw_exit()


func _draw_background() -> void:
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), fill_color)
	var grid_color := Color(0.35, 0.5, 0.65, 0.07)
	for x in range(40, 961, 40):
		draw_line(Vector2(x, 210), Vector2(x, 540), grid_color)
	for y in range(210, 541, 40):
		draw_line(Vector2(0, y), Vector2(960, y), grid_color)
	draw_circle(Vector2(795, 240), 44.0, Color(0.12, 0.2, 0.29, 0.5))
	draw_circle(Vector2(795, 240), 31.0, fill_color)


func _draw_platform() -> void:
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), fill_color)
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(shape_size.x, 4.0)), accent_color)
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), accent_color.darkened(0.5), false, 1.0)
	var bolt_color := accent_color.darkened(0.4)
	draw_circle(Vector2(12.0, 14.0), 2.0, bolt_color)
	draw_circle(Vector2(shape_size.x - 12.0, 14.0), 2.0, bolt_color)


func _draw_player() -> void:
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), fill_color)
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), accent_color, false, 1.0)
	draw_rect(Rect2(4.0, 8.0, shape_size.x - 8.0, 6.0), Color(0.13, 0.19, 0.25))
	draw_rect(Rect2(4.0, 25.0, 5.0, 7.0), fill_color.darkened(0.25))
	draw_rect(Rect2(shape_size.x - 9.0, 25.0, 5.0, 7.0), fill_color.darkened(0.25))


func _draw_exit() -> void:
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), fill_color)
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), accent_color, false, 2.0)
	draw_rect(Rect2(6.0, 7.0, shape_size.x - 12.0, shape_size.y - 7.0), fill_color.darkened(0.3))
	draw_circle(Vector2(shape_size.x - 11.0, shape_size.y * 0.55), 2.5, accent_color)

	# jump: only a fresh press on a supporting platform starts a jump.
	velocity.y += GRAVITY * delta
	if jump_pressed and is_on_floor():
		velocity.y = -jump_speed
	# platform-collision: use the scene's matching solid collision rectangles.
	move_and_slide()


func stop_motion() -> void:
	controls_enabled = false
	velocity = Vector2.ZERO

## Object procedural-rendering: drawing only, with no collision or input logic.

@export_enum("background", "platform", "player", "exit")
var shape_kind: String = "platform"
@export var shape_size: Vector2 = Vector2.ZERO

		"platform":

		"player":

		"exit":

func _draw_background() -> void:
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), fill_color)
	var grid_color := Color(0.35, 0.5, 0.65, 0.07)
	for x in range(40, 961, 40):

	for y in range(210, 541, 40):

	draw_circle(Vector2(795, 240), 44.0, Color(0.12, 0.2, 0.29, 0.5))
	draw_circle(Vector2(795, 240), 31.0, fill_color)


func _draw_platform() -> void:
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), fill_color)
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(shape_size.x, 4.0)), accent_color)
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), accent_color.darkened(0.5), false, 1.0)
	var bolt_color := accent_color.darkened(0.4)
	draw_circle(Vector2(12.0, 14.0), 2.0, bolt_color)

	draw_rect(Rect2(4.0, 8.0, shape_size.x - 8.0, 6.0), Color(0.13, 0.19, 0.25))
	draw_rect(Rect2(4.0, 25.0, 5.0, 7.0), fill_color.darkened(0.25))
	draw_rect(Rect2(shape_size.x - 9.0, 25.0, 5.0, 7.0), fill_color.darkened(0.25))


func _draw_exit() -> void:
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), fill_color)
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), accent_color, false, 2.0)
	draw_rect(Rect2(6.0, 7.0, shape_size.x - 12.0, shape_size.y - 7.0), fill_color.darkened(0.3))
	draw_circle(Vector2(shape_size.x - 11.0, shape_size.y * 0.55), 2.5, accent_color)

Implemented Bridge Runner across `project.godot`, `scenes/main.tscn`, and six scripts: `input_actions.gd`, `player.gd`, `level_controller.gd`, `view_setup.gd`, `procedural_visuals.gd`, and `hud.gd`.

Added all declared objects and mechanisms: keyboard controls, three solid platforms, green exit, win/fall/reset behavior, fixed view, procedural visuals, and HUD. Player parameters use the protected runtime accessor; stable IDs and source bindings are explicit.

Godot, tests, and checksums were not run. Backend verification and human playtesting remain pending; this isolated implementation has no production approval.

objects.description: A self-contained Godot 4 GDScript 2D MVP with a single playable level.
objects.name: Bridge Runner

objects.description: Contains the player, three platforms, exit, procedural renderer, and HUD. Coordinates level state and restart behavior.
objects.name: Main Scene

objects.description: Define move_left for Left Arrow, move_right for Right Arrow, jump for Space, and reset_level for R. Translate input into movement, jump, and reset intent.
objects.name: Keyboard Input Actions

objects.description: A 24x32 rectangular CharacterBody2D. Start centered at (100, 414) on the first platform. Read speed and jump-speed from the frozen fields through StudioRuntime.object_value().
objects.name: Player

objects.description: Apply left/right intent using the player's speed field. Stop horizontal movement when neither direction is held; opposing inputs cancel.
objects.name: Horizontal Movement

objects.description: A fresh Space press while grounded sets upward velocity from jump-speed. Apply gravity of 1000 px/s² during physics updates. Holding Space does not cause repeated jumps.
objects.name: Grounded Jump

objects.description: A visible solid rectangle at (40, 430), sized 260x24 pixels. Holds the initial player spawn.
objects.name: Starting Platform

objects.description: A visible solid rectangle at (370, 350), sized 210x24 pixels. Provides the intermediate jump destination.
objects.name: Middle Platform

objects.description: A visible solid rectangle at (650, 410), sized 270x24 pixels. Supports the green exit.
objects.name: Exit Platform

objects.description: Use static platform collision shapes matching the rendered rectangles. Player physics handles landing and grounded detection. Gaps remain open, with no invisible floor.
objects.name: Solid Platform Collision

objects.description: A green rectangular Area2D at (860, 350), sized 40x60 pixels, resting on the third platform. Label it EXIT.
objects.name: Green Exit

objects.description: When the player overlaps the exit during play, enter the won state, stop player motion, and display the win message and R restart instruction.
objects.name: Reach Exit

objects.description: During play, restart when the player's center passes y=600. Return to the initial spawn and clear velocity and level state.
objects.name: Fall Restart

objects.description: R restores the initial level state from either playing or won state, including spawn, zero velocity, active controls, and the normal HUD.
objects.name: R Reset

objects.description: Maintain playing and won states. Use one restart path for falling and R. Evaluate reset before other transitions; suppress falling and movement after winning until reset.
objects.name: Level State

objects.description: Use a fixed 960x540 logical viewport showing the entire level. Do not follow the player or scroll. Preserve aspect ratio when the window changes size.
objects.name: Fixed View

objects.description: Render the background, player, platforms, and green exit using simple Godot shapes and colors. Keep drawing separate from physics, input handling, and HUD text.
objects.name: Procedural Shapes

objects.description: Show: Left/Right: move | Space: jump | R: reset. Explain the goal: Cross the platforms to the green exit. On victory, show: You win! Press R to restart. Keep text clear of the jump route.
objects.name: Controls and Win HUD

userAcceptance.text: Implement one Godot 4 GDScript 2D level with procedural visuals, no sound, no external assets or plugins, and no network access.
The main-scene object is bound to scenes/main.tscn. Keep every declared object and mechanism associated with its listed source bindings.

Preserve player field IDs speed and jump-speed. Speed is editable numeric data with value 220, minimum 50, maximum 500. Jump-speed is editable numeric data with value 420, minimum 200, maximum 700. Game source reads these frozen values through StudioRuntime.object_value(). Do not modify backend-owned design/game.json or studio/runtime.gd.
Left and Right Arrow move the player horizontally; Space triggers a grounded jump; R resets the level. Opposing direction inputs cancel, and holding Space does not produce repeated jumps.

Show exactly three solid platforms simultaneously. At the default player field values, the player can jump from the starting platform to the middle platform and then to the exit platform. Manually assess reachability and adjust platform spacing if needed while retaining the specified player defaults.
The player lands reliably on matching platform collision shapes and can fall through the open gaps. Grounded detection permits jumping only while supported.
Place a clearly visible green exit on the third platform. Player overlap changes the level to won, stops player movement, and displays a win message with an R restart instruction.

requirements.text: Implement one Godot 4 GDScript 2D level with procedural visuals, no sound, no external assets or plugins, and no network access.
The main-scene object is bound to scenes/main.tscn. Keep every declared object and mechanism associated with its listed source bindings.

Preserve player field IDs speed and jump-speed. Speed is editable numeric data with value 300, minimum 50, maximum 500. Jump-speed is editable numeric data with value 420, minimum 200, maximum 700. Game source reads these frozen values through StudioRuntime.object_value(). Do not modify backend-owned design/game.json or studio/runtime.gd.
Left and Right Arrow move the player horizontally; Space triggers a grounded jump; R resets the level. Opposing direction inputs cancel, and holding Space does not produce repeated jumps.

Show exactly three solid platforms simultaneously. Preserve their existing positions and sizes. With speed 300 px/s and jump-speed 420 px/s, the player should be able to jump from the starting platform to the middle platform and then to the exit platform. Manually assess reachability and report any concern without changing the platforms.
The player lands reliably on matching platform collision shapes and can fall through the open gaps. Grounded detection permits jumping only while supported.
Place a clearly visible green exit on the third platform. Player overlap changes the level to won, stops player movement, and displays a win message with an R restart instruction.
Falling below the level during play automatically restores the initial spawn, zero velocity, playing state, and normal HUD.
R restores the same initial state during play and after winning. The player can complete another attempt after either reset path.
Use a fixed 960x540 logical view with all three platforms and the exit visible together. The view does not follow the player or scroll.
The HUD explains arrow movement, Space jumping, R reset, and the green-exit goal. Win feedback is readable and does not obscure the platform route.
Keep physics and level simulation separate from input action mapping, procedural rendering, and interface updates. Input supplies intent; rendering reflects state; HUD presents controls and outcomes.
Render the player cyan (#00FFFF) to make it easier to track. Preserve its 24x32 dimensions, collision shape, and initial spawn. Preserve all other existing visual elements.
Limit the requested change to player speed 300 px/s and cyan player rendering. Preserve existing platforms, controls, jump speed, gravity, collisions, exit behavior, reset paths, fixed view, and HUD.

requirements.text: Implement one Godot 4 GDScript 2D level with procedural visuals, no sound, no external assets or plugins, and no network access.
The main-scene object is bound to scenes/main.tscn. Keep every declared object and mechanism associated with its listed source bindings.

Preserve player field IDs speed and jump-speed. Speed is editable numeric data with value 300, minimum 50, maximum 500. Jump-speed is editable numeric data with value 420, minimum 200, maximum 700. Game source reads these frozen values through StudioRuntime.object_value(). Do not modify backend-owned design/game.json or studio/runtime.gd.
Left and Right Arrow move the player horizontally; Space triggers a grounded jump; R resets the level. Opposing direction inputs cancel, and holding Space does not produce repeated jumps.

Show exactly three solid platforms simultaneously. Preserve their existing positions and sizes. With speed 300 px/s and jump-speed 420 px/s, the player should be able to jump from the starting platform to the middle platform and then to the exit platform. Manually assess reachability and report any concern without changing the platforms.
The player lands reliably on matching platform collision shapes and can fall through the open gaps. Grounded detection permits jumping only while supported.
Place a clearly visible green exit on the third platform. Player overlap changes the level to won, stops player movement, and displays a win message with an R restart instruction.
Falling below the level during play automatically restores the initial spawn, zero velocity, playing state, and normal HUD.
R restores the same initial state during play and after winning. The player can complete another attempt after either reset path.
Use a fixed 960x540 logical view with all three platforms and the exit visible together. The view does not follow the player or scroll.
The HUD explains arrow movement, Space jumping, R reset, and the green-exit goal. Win feedback is readable and does not obscure the platform route.
Keep physics and level simulation separate from input action mapping, procedural rendering, and interface updates. Input supplies intent; rendering reflects state; HUD presents controls and outcomes.
Render the player cyan (#00FFFF) to make it easier to track. Preserve its 24x32 dimensions, collision shape, and initial spawn. Preserve all other existing visual elements.
Limit the requested change to player speed 300 px/s and cyan player rendering. Preserve existing platforms, controls, jump speed, gravity, collisions, exit behavior, reset paths, fixed view, and HUD.

document.summary: A small Godot 4 GDScript side-view jump game. Move the cyan player at 300 px/s with the left/right arrow keys and jump with Space to cross three visible platforms and reach a green exit. Preserve the existing platforms and controls. Falling restarts the level, and R resets it at any time. Use a fixed 960x540 view, procedural shapes, one level, and no sound, external assets, plugins, or network access. Keep simulation, input actions, rendering, and interface responsibilities separate.

## Concept
A small Godot 4 GDScript side-view jump game. Move the cyan player at 300 px/s with the left/right arrow keys and jump with Space to cross three visible platforms and reach a green exit. Preserve the existing platforms and controls. Falling restarts the level, and R resets it at any time. - `player` (entity): Player. A 24x32 rectangular CharacterBody2D rendered cyan (#00FFFF) so it is easier to track. Start centered at (100, 414) on the first platform. Read speed and jump-speed from the frozen fields through StudioRuntime.object_value(). Sources: scenes/main.tscn, scripts/player.gd.

- `player.jump-speed` (number): Jump Speed; current value `420`; editable `true`.
- `horizontal-movement` (mechanic): Horizontal Movement. Apply left/right intent using the player's speed field. Stop horizontal movement when neither direction is held; opposing inputs cancel. Sources: scripts/player.gd.
- `jump` (mechanic): Grounded Jump. A fresh Space press while grounded sets upward velocity from jump-speed. Apply gravity of 1000 px/s² during physics updates. Holding Space does not cause repeated jumps. Sources: scripts/player.gd.
- `platform-one` (entity): Starting Platform. A visible solid rectangle at (40, 430), sized 260x24 pixels. Holds the initial player spawn. Sources: scenes/main.tscn.

extends CharacterBody2D

## Object player; mechanisms horizontal-movement, jump, platform-collision.
## The controller supplies intent and owns the timing of each simulation step.
const OBJECT_ID := "player"
const MECHANISM_IDS := ["horizontal-movement", "jump", "platform-collision"]
const GRAVITY := 1000.0
const RuntimeSource = preload("res://studio/runtime.gd")

var speed: float = 0.0
var jump_speed: float = 0.0
var controls_enabled: bool = false
var _studio_runtime = RuntimeSource.new()


func reset_to(spawn: Vector2) -> void:
	global_position = spawn
	velocity = Vector2.ZERO
	# Read the authoritative fields on startup and on both restart paths.
	# Do not duplicate their defaults or ranges in game source.
	var speed_value: Variant = _studio_runtime.object_value(OBJECT_ID, "speed")
	var jump_value: Variant = _studio_runtime.object_value(OBJECT_ID, "jump-speed")
	controls_enabled = (
		(speed_value is int or speed_value is float)
		and (jump_value is int or jump_value is float)
	)
	if not controls_enabled:
		push_error("Player requires numeric speed and jump-speed fields in design/game.json.")
		return
	speed = float(speed_value)
	jump_speed = float(jump_value)


func simulate(delta: float, direction: float, jump_pressed: bool) -> void:
	if not controls_enabled:
		return
	# horizontal-movement: immediate start/stop, with no residual drift.
	velocity.x = direction * speed
	# jump: only a fresh press on a supporting platform starts a jump.
	velocity.y += GRAVITY * delta
	if jump_pressed and is_on_floor():
		velocity.y = -jump_speed
	# platform-collision: use the scene's matching solid collision rectangles.
	move_and_slide()


func stop_motion() -> void:
	controls_enabled = false
	velocity = Vector2.ZERO
extends Node2D

## Object procedural-rendering: drawing only, with no collision or input logic.
## Visual children inherit their entity's transform from scenes/main.tscn.
const OBJECT_ID := "procedural-rendering"

@export_enum("background", "platform", "player", "exit")
var shape_kind: String = "platform"
@export var shape_size: Vector2 = Vector2.ZERO
@export var fill_color: Color = Color.WHITE
@export var accent_color: Color = Color.WHITE


func _draw() -> void:
	match shape_kind:
		"background":
			_draw_background()
		"platform":
			_draw_platform()
		"player":
			_draw_player()
		"exit":
			_draw_exit()


func _draw_background() -> void:
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), fill_color)
	var grid_color := Color(0.35, 0.5, 0.65, 0.07)
	for x in range(40, 961, 40):
		draw_line(Vector2(x, 210), Vector2(x, 540), grid_color)
	for y in range(210, 541, 40):
		draw_line(Vector2(0, y), Vector2(960, y), grid_color)
	draw_circle(Vector2(795, 240), 44.0, Color(0.12, 0.2, 0.29, 0.5))
	draw_circle(Vector2(795, 240), 31.0, fill_color)


func _draw_platform() -> void:
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), fill_color)
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(shape_size.x, 4.0)), accent_color)
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), accent_color.darkened(0.5), false, 1.0)
	var bolt_color := accent_color.darkened(0.4)
	draw_circle(Vector2(12.0, 14.0), 2.0, bolt_color)
	draw_circle(Vector2(shape_size.x - 12.0, 14.0), 2.0, bolt_color)


func _draw_player() -> void:
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), fill_color)
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), accent_color, false, 1.0)
	draw_rect(Rect2(4.0, 8.0, shape_size.x - 8.0, 6.0), Color(0.13, 0.19, 0.25))
	draw_rect(Rect2(4.0, 25.0, 5.0, 7.0), fill_color.darkened(0.25))
	draw_rect(Rect2(shape_size.x - 9.0, 25.0, 5.0, 7.0), fill_color.darkened(0.25))


func _draw_exit() -> void:
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), fill_color)
	draw_rect(Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, shape_size), accent_color, false, 2.0)
	draw_rect(Rect2(6.0, 7.0, shape_size.x - 12.0, shape_size.y - 7.0), fill_color.darkened(0.3))
	draw_circle(Vector2(shape_size.x - 11.0, shape_size.y * 0.55), 2.5, accent_color)

## Game Description
A small Godot 4 GDScript side-view jump game. Move the cyan player at 300 px/s with the left/right arrow keys and jump with Space to cross three visible platforms and reach a green exit. Preserve the existing platforms and controls. Falling restarts the level, and R resets it at any time. Use a fixed 960x540 view, procedural shapes, one level, and no sound, external assets, plugins, or network access. Keep simulation, input actions, rendering, and interface responsibilities separate. class_name StudioRuntime

## Protected bridge from game code to the server-owned object document.
## Generated game scripts should read declared values through this API.

static func value(document: Dictionary, object_id: String, field_id: String, default_value: Variant = null) -> Variant:
	for object_value in document.get("objects", []):
		if not object_value is Dictionary or object_value.get("id") != object_id:
			continue
		for field_value in object_value.get("fields", []):
			if field_value is Dictionary and field_value.get("id") == field_id:
				return field_value.get("value", default_value)
	return default_value


func object_value(object_id: String, field_id: String, default_value: Variant = null) -> Variant:
	var file := FileAccess.open("res://design/game.json", FileAccess.READ)
	if file == null:
		return default_value
	var parsed: Variant = JSON.parse_string(file.get_as_text())
	if not parsed is Dictionary:
		return default_value
	return value(parsed, object_id, field_id, default_value)

userAcceptance.text: Implement one Godot 4 GDScript 2D level with procedural visuals, no sound, no external assets or plugins, and no network access.
The main-scene object is bound to scenes/main.tscn. Keep every declared object and mechanism associated with its listed source bindings.

Preserve player field IDs speed and jump-speed. Speed is editable numeric data with value 300, minimum 50, maximum 500. Jump-speed is editable numeric data with value 420, minimum 200, maximum 700. Game source reads these frozen values through StudioRuntime.object_value(). Do not modify backend-owned design/game.json or studio/runtime.gd.
Left and Right Arrow move the player horizontally; Space triggers a grounded jump; R resets the level. Opposing direction inputs cancel, and holding Space does not produce repeated jumps.

Show exactly three solid platforms simultaneously. Preserve their existing positions and sizes. With speed 300 px/s and jump-speed 420 px/s, the player should be able to jump from the starting platform to the middle platform and then to the exit platform. requirements.text: Implement one local Godot 4 GDScript 2D puzzle. Use procedural visuals and native controls only. Exclude external assets, plugins, network access, audio, additional levels, persistence, and export packaging from this MVP.
Run in a fixed, non-resizable 960×540 window. Keep the complete board, title, instructions, move counter, Reset button, and win message visible without scrolling or overlap.

Display exactly nine evenly spaced square buttons as a centered 3×3 grid. Each button shows its current ON or OFF state. Provide clear hover and pressed feedback while retaining readable state labels.

Before a win, one mouse activation toggles the selected cell and each in-bounds orthogonal neighbor exactly once. Do not toggle diagonal cells or wrap at edges. A corner affects three cells, an edge-center affects four, and the center affects five.

Generate the fixed start from nine OFF cells by applying the toggle rule to (0,0), (1,1), and (2,2), in order, using zero-based row and column coordinates. The required starting state has only the main diagonal ON. Seeding does not count as player moves. Replaying these three selections is the documented solution.
Display Moves: 0 on launch and reset. Increment the count once for each accepted cell activation, regardless of how many lights change. Preserve the final count when the puzzle is won.
Detect a win when all nine lights are OFF after a player move. Show All lights out! and retain the final move count. Disable further cell activations until reset; keep both reset controls available.

The Reset button and the R key invoke the same reset operation before and after winning. Reset reconstructs the fixed starting board, sets moves to zero, clears the win message, and enables cell input. Ignore repeated key events from holding R. R must work when a board button or Reset has focus.

Show the title Light Grid and concise instructions explaining that clicking toggles a square and its orthogonal neighbors, the goal is all lights OFF, and R resets. Keep the move counter and Reset button visible throughout play.

Expose puzzle-board.accent-color as the editable choice field defined in this document. Game source obtains its frozen value through StudioRuntime.object_value() and uses the selected hexadecimal color for lit squares. Each supported choice must retain readable labels and a clear distinction from unlit squares.

Use scripts/rules.gd for simulation, scripts/puzzle_board.gd for board rendering, scripts/puzzle_input.gd for routing cell selections and the R reset input action, scripts/hud.gd for interface rendering and reset requests, and scripts/main.gd for coordination. Bind the main scene to scenes/main.tscn. Keep input and interface code from directly mutating the rules' board state.

Later manual review must inspect the initial diagonal pattern; check corner, edge-center, and center toggles from fresh resets; check one move per activation; solve with (0,0), (1,1), (2,2) and inspect the three-move win; check post-win input lock; exercise both reset controls during play and after winning; and inspect each accent choice. Record observed results without claiming formal verification.

# Game Design Document — Light Grid

## Concept
A small 2D puzzle in a fixed 960×540 window. Clicking a square toggles its light and its orthogonal neighbors. Turn every light off to win. Display moves, concise instructions, a Reset button, and a win message. Use procedural squares and labels without external assets, plugins, network, or audio.

## Object Model
- `main-scene` (scene): Light Grid Main Scene. Owns scene composition and coordinates input, puzzle state, board rendering, and HUD updates. Input actions are handled separately in puzzle_input.gd. Sources: scenes/main.tscn, scripts/main.gd, scripts/puzzle_input.gd.
- `puzzle-board` (entity): Puzzle Board. Renders nine square buttons in three rows and three columns. Emits cell selections and displays state supplied by the rules. Lit squares use the chosen accent; unlit squares use a dark neutral fill. ON and OFF labels distinguish states independently of color. Sources: scripts/puzzle_board.gd.
- `puzzle-board.accent-color` (choice): Accent color; current value `"#38BDF8"`; editable `true`.
- `rules` (rule): Lights Out Rules. Owns the nine light states, legal toggles, deterministic start generation, move count, solved detection, and reset. Contains no rendering or input handling. Sources: scripts/rules.gd.
- `hud` (interface): Puzzle HUD. Displays Light Grid, instructions, move count, Reset, and the win message. Emits reset requests without mutating puzzle state. Sources: scripts/hud.gd.

## Requirements
- `project-scope`: Implement one local Godot 4 GDScript 2D puzzle. Use procedural visuals and native controls only. Exclude external assets, plugins, network access, audio, additional levels, persistence, and export packaging from this MVP. (objects: main-scene, puzzle-board, rules, hud; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `fixed-window`: Run in a fixed, non-resizable 960×540 window. Keep the complete board, title, instructions, move counter, Reset button, and win message visible without scrolling or overlap. (objects: main-scene, puzzle-board, hud; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `board-layout`: Display exactly nine evenly spaced square buttons as a centered 3×3 grid. Each button shows its current ON or OFF state. Provide clear hover and pressed feedback while retaining readable state labels. (objects: puzzle-board; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `toggle-rule`: Before a win, one mouse activation toggles the selected cell and each in-bounds orthogonal neighbor exactly once. Do not toggle diagonal cells or wrap at edges. A corner affects three cells, an edge-center affects four, and the center affects five. (objects: puzzle-board, rules; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `solvable-start`: Generate the fixed start from nine OFF cells by applying the toggle rule to (0,0), (1,1), and (2,2), in order, using zero-based row and column coordinates. The required starting state has only the main diagonal ON. Seeding does not count as player moves. Replaying these three selections is the documented solution. (objects: rules; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `move-count`: Display Moves: 0 on launch and reset. Increment the count once for each accepted cell activation, regardless of how many lights change. Preserve the final count when the puzzle is won. (objects: rules, hud; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `win-state`: Detect a win when all nine lights are OFF after a player move. Show All lights out! and retain the final move count. Disable further cell activations until reset; keep both reset controls available. (objects: rules, puzzle-board, hud; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `reset-controls`: The Reset button and the R key invoke the same reset operation before and after winning. Reset reconstructs the fixed starting board, sets moves to zero, clears the win message, and enables cell input. Ignore repeated key events from holding R. R must work when a board button or Reset has focus. (objects: main-scene, puzzle-board, rules, hud; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `hud-content`: Show the title Light Grid and concise instructions explaining that clicking toggles a square and its orthogonal neighbors, the goal is all lights OFF, and R resets. Keep the move counter and Reset button visible throughout play. (objects: hud; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `editable-accent`: Expose puzzle-board.accent-color as the editable choice field defined in this document. Game source obtains its frozen value through StudioRuntime.object_value() and uses the selected hexadecimal color for lit squares. Each supported choice must retain readable labels and a clear distinction from unlit squares. (objects: puzzle-board; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `separate-responsibilities`: Use scripts/rules.gd for simulation, scripts/puzzle_board.gd for board rendering, scripts/puzzle_input.gd for routing cell selections and the R reset input action, scripts/hud.gd for interface rendering and reset requests, and scripts/main.gd for coordination. Bind the main scene to scenes/main.tscn. Keep input and interface code from directly mutating the rules' board state. (objects: main-scene, puzzle-board, rules, hud; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).
- `manual-gameplay-review`: Later manual review must inspect the initial diagonal pattern; check corner, edge-center, and center toggles from fresh resets; check one move per activation; solve with (0,0), (1,1), (2,2) and inspect the three-move win; check post-win input lock; exercise both reset controls during play and after winning; and inspect each accent choice. Record observed results without claiming formal verification. (objects: main-scene, puzzle-board, rules, hud; requested check: manual; verification state: pending).

## Scope and Evidence
The object document is the structured source of intent. Planning questions must be resolved before implementation. Technical smoke cannot claim unobserved game behavior; human acceptance remains a separate user decision.

class_name StudioRuntime

## Protected bridge from game code to the server-owned object document.
## Generated game scripts should read declared values through this API.

static func value(document: Dictionary, object_id: String, field_id: String, default_value: Variant = null) -> Variant:
	for object_value in document.get("objects", []):
		if not object_value is Dictionary or object_value.get("id") != object_id:
			continue
		for field_value in object_value.get("fields", []):
			if field_value is Dictionary and field_value.get("id") == field_id:
				return field_value.get("value", default_value)
	return default_value


func object_value(object_id: String, field_id: String, default_value: Variant = null) -> Variant:
	var file := FileAccess.open("res://design/game.json", FileAccess.READ)
	if file == null:
		return default_value
	var parsed: Variant = JSON.parse_string(file.get_as_text())
	if not parsed is Dictionary:
		return default_value
	return value(parsed, object_id, field_id, default_value)

extends Node

## rules: simulation only. Coordinates are zero-based (row, column).
## Start and documented solution: (0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 2).

const GRID_SIZE: int = 3
const CELL_COUNT: int = GRID_SIZE * GRID_SIZE
const START_SEQUENCE = [Vector2i(0, 0), Vector2i(1, 1), Vector2i(2, 2)]
const CROSS_OFFSETS = [
	Vector2i.ZERO,
	Vector2i.UP,
	Vector2i.DOWN,
	Vector2i.LEFT,
	Vector2i.RIGHT,
]

var _cells: Array[bool] = []
var _move_count: int = 0
var _solved: bool = false


func _init() -> void:
	reset()


func reset() -> void:
	_cells.resize(CELL_COUNT)
	_cells.fill(false)
	_move_count = 0
	_solved = false
	# Seed through the same cross rule without recording player moves.
	for selection in START_SEQUENCE:
		_toggle_cross(selection.x, selection.y)


func activate_cell(row: int, column: int) -> bool:
	if _solved or not _is_in_bounds(row, column):
		return false
	_toggle_cross(row, column)
	_move_count += 1
	_solved = not _cells.has(true)
	return true


func get_cells() -> Array[bool]:
	# A snapshot prevents views or input code from mutating the model's array.
	return _cells.duplicate()


func get_move_count() -> int:
	return _move_count


func is_solved() -> bool:
	return _solved


func _toggle_cross(row: int, column: int) -> void:
	for offset in CROSS_OFFSETS:
		var neighbor_row: int = row + offset.y
		var neighbor_column: int = column + offset.x
		if _is_in_bounds(neighbor_row, neighbor_column):
			var index: int = neighbor_row * GRID_SIZE + neighbor_column
			_cells[index] = not _cells[index]


func _is_in_bounds(row: int, column: int) -> bool:
	return row >= 0 and row < GRID_SIZE and column >= 0 and column < GRID_SIZE

const GRID_SIZE: int = 3
const CELL_COUNT: int = GRID_SIZE * GRID_SIZE
const START_SEQUENCE = [Vector2i(0, 0), Vector2i(1, 1), Vector2i(2, 2)]
const CROSS_OFFSETS = [
	Vector2i.ZERO,
	Vector2i.UP,
	Vector2i.DOWN,
	Vector2i.LEFT,
	Vector2i.RIGHT,
]

var _cells: Array[bool] = []
var _move_count: int = 0
var _solved: bool = false

	reset()


func reset() -> void:
	_cells.resize(CELL_COUNT)
	_cells.fill(false)
	_move_count = 0
	_solved = false
	# Seed through the same cross rule without recording player moves.
	for selection in START_SEQUENCE:
		_toggle_cross(selection.x, selection.y)


func activate_cell(row: int, column: int) -> bool:
	if _solved or not _is_in_bounds(row, column):
		return false
	_toggle_cross(row, column)
	_move_count += 1
	_solved = not _cells.has(true)
	return true


func get_cells() -> Array[bool]:
	# A snapshot prevents views or input code from mutating the model's array.

func get_move_count() -> int:

func _toggle_cross(row: int, column: int) -> void:
	for offset in CROSS_OFFSETS:
		var neighbor_row: int = row + offset.y
		var neighbor_column: int = column + offset.x
		if _is_in_bounds(neighbor_row, neighbor_column):

			_cells[index] = not _cells[index]


func _is_in_bounds(row: int, column: int) -> bool:
	return row >= 0 and row < GRID_SIZE and column >= 0 and column < GRID_SIZE

const StudioRuntimeSource = preload("res://studio/runtime.gd")
const GRID_SIZE: int = 3
const CELL_SIDE: float = 88.0
const CELL_GAP: int = 10
const OFF_FILL: Color = Color("#1E293B")
const OFF_BORDER: Color = Color("#475569")

const OFF_TEXT: Color = Color("#E2E8F0")

var _buttons: Array[Button] = []
var _lit_styles: Dictionary = {}
var _off_styles: Dictionary = {}


func _ready() -> void:
	var runtime := StudioRuntimeSource.new()
	var accent_hex: String = str(runtime.object_value("puzzle-board", "accent-color", ""))
	if not Color.html_is_valid(accent_hex):
		push_error("Light Grid: puzzle-board.accent-color must be a valid design color.")
	var accent: Color = Color.from_string(accent_hex, Color.WHITE)
	_lit_styles = _make_styles(accent, accent.darkened(0.18))
	_off_styles = _make_styles(OFF_FILL, OFF_BORDER)
	columns = GRID_SIZE
	add_theme_constant_override("h_separation", CELL_GAP)
	add_theme_constant_override("v_separation", CELL_GAP)
	for row in range(GRID_SIZE):
		for column in range(GRID_SIZE):
			_create_cell(row, column)


func render_state(cells: Array[bool], solved: bool) -> void:
	for index in range(_buttons.size()):
		var button: Button = _buttons[index]
		var lit: bool = cells[index]
		var styles: Dictionary = _lit_styles if lit else _off_styles
		var text_color: Color = LIT_TEXT if lit else OFF_TEXT
		button.text = "ON" if lit else "OFF"
		button.disabled = solved
		button.mouse_default_cursor_shape = (
			Control.CURSOR_ARROW if solved else Control.CURSOR_POINTING_HAND
		)
		for style_name in styles:
			button.add_theme_stylebox_override(style_name, styles[style_name])
		for color_name in [
			&"font_color", &"font_hover_color", &"font_pressed_color",
			&"font_focus_color", &"font_disabled_color", &"font_hover_pressed_color",
		]:
			button.add_theme_color_override(color_name, text_color)


func _create_cell(row: int, column: int) -> void:
	var button := Button.new()
	button.name = "Cell_%d_%d" % [row, column]
	button.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(CELL_SIDE, CELL_SIDE)
	button.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_SHRINK_CENTER
	button.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_SHRINK_CENTER
	button.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_ALL
	button.mouse_default_cursor_shape = Control.CURSOR_POINTING_HAND
	button.text = "OFF"
	button.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 20)
	button.tooltip_text = "Row %d, column %d: toggle this square and its orthogonal neighbors." % [
		row + 1, column + 1,
	]
	button.pressed.connect(_on_cell_pressed.bind(row, column))
	_buttons.append(button)
	add_child(button)


func _on_cell_pressed(row: int, column: int) -> void:
	cell_selected.emit(row, column)


func _make_styles(fill: Color, border: Color) -> Dictionary:
	var focus := _make_style(Color.TRANSPARENT, Color.WHITE, 2)
	focus.draw_center = false
	focus.expand_margin_left = 3.0
	focus.expand_margin_top = 3.0
	focus.expand_margin_right = 3.0
	focus.expand_margin_bottom = 3.0
	return {
		&"normal": _make_style(fill, border, 2),
		&"hover": _make_style(fill.lightened(0.14), Color.WHITE, 3),
		&"pressed": _make_style(fill.darkened(0.14), Color.WHITE, 3),
		&"disabled": _make_style(fill, border, 2),
		&"focus": focus,
	}


func _make_style(fill: Color, border: Color, border_width: int) -> StyleBoxFlat:
	var style := StyleBoxFlat.new()
	style.bg_color = fill
	style.border_color = border
	style.set_border_width_all(border_width)
	style.set_corner_radius_all(10)
	return style

userAcceptance.text: Implement one local Godot 4 GDScript 2D puzzle. Use procedural visuals and native controls only. Exclude external assets, plugins, network access, audio, additional levels, persistence, and export packaging from this MVP.
Run in a fixed, non-resizable 960×540 window. Keep the complete board, title, instructions, move counter, Reset button, and win message visible without scrolling or overlap.

Display exactly nine evenly spaced square buttons as a centered 3×3 grid. Each button shows its current ON or OFF state. Provide clear hover and pressed feedback while retaining readable state labels.

Before a win, one mouse activation toggles the selected cell and each in-bounds orthogonal neighbor exactly once. Do not toggle diagonal cells or wrap at edges. A corner affects three cells, an edge-center affects four, and the center affects five.

Generate the fixed start from nine OFF cells by applying the toggle rule to (0,0), (1,1), and (2,2), in order, using zero-based row and column coordinates. The required starting state has only the main diagonal ON. Seeding does not count as player moves. Replaying these three selections is the documented solution.
Display Moves: 0 on launch and reset. Increment the count once for each accepted cell activation, regardless of how many lights change. Preserve the final count when the puzzle is won.
Detect a win when all nine lights are OFF after a player move. Show All lights out! and retain the final move count. Disable further cell activations until reset; keep both reset controls available.

The Reset button and the R key invoke the same reset operation before and after winning. Reset reconstructs the fixed starting board, sets moves to zero, clears the win message, and enables cell input. Ignore repeated key events from holding R. R must work when a board button or Reset has focus.

Show the title Light Grid and concise instructions explaining that clicking toggles a square and its orthogonal neighbors, the goal is all lights OFF, and R resets. Keep the move counter and Reset button visible throughout play.

Expose puzzle-board.accent-color as the editable choice field defined in this document. Game source obtains its frozen value through StudioRuntime.object_value() and uses the selected hexadecimal color for lit squares. Each supported choice must retain readable labels and a clear distinction from unlit squares.

Use scripts/rules.gd for simulation, scripts/puzzle_board.gd for board rendering, scripts/puzzle_input.gd for routing cell selections and the R reset input action, scripts/hud.gd for interface rendering and reset requests, and scripts/main.gd for coordination. Bind the main scene to scenes/main.tscn. Keep input and interface code from directly mutating the rules' board state.

Later manual review must inspect the initial diagonal pattern; check corner, edge-center, and center toggles from fresh resets; check one move per activation; solve with (0,0), (1,1), (2,2) and inspect the three-move win; check post-win input lock; exercise both reset controls during play and after winning; and inspect each accent choice. Record observed results without claiming formal verification.
